note: Pass criteria marked 'Proposed' are suggestions for the maintainer to confirm. A result counts as hardware only when it was run on real hardware and says so (see docs/TESTING.md).

areas.title: Rendering, shaders and 3D scenes on graphics card vendors

automated.note: compiles every shader on the driver in use
renders every effect and checks the picture
loads and draws the 3D test models
frame times of all factory looks; on software OpenGL these numbers say nothing about a real card

manual.title: Shader compile, selftests and look benchmark on one graphics card
manual.needs: A Windows or Linux PC with one NVIDIA, AMD or Intel graphics card and its current vendor driver
steps: Start a command line in the folder of NyrexVJ.
Run the three selftests (A-RENDER-2 to A-RENDER-4) and note every line that says FAILED.
Run A-RENDER-5 with --bench-budget 16.7 and keep OUT.json.
Write the GL_RENDERER string from OUT.json and the driver version into the result.
manual.measure: Shader failures, selftest exit codes, avg/p95/p99/max work time per look from OUT.json
manual.criteria: Proposed: no shader failure, all three selftests exit 0, every factory look passes the 16.7 ms budget at 1080p. The maintainer sets the real thresholds.

areas.title: Spout output to OBS, Unreal or VRChat capture (Windows)

automated.note: output chain with a fake NDI library; Spout itself only compiles on Windows

manual.title: Spout sender seen by a real receiver
manual.needs: Windows PC with a graphics card and OBS (Spout plugin) or another Spout receiver
steps: Start NyrexVJ with a visible look and turn Spout output on.
Open the receiver and select the NyrexVJ sender.
Run scripts/measure_live.py for 10 minutes while the look plays.
Stop and start NyrexVJ twice and check that the receiver finds the sender again.
manual.measure: Picture correct (orientation, colours), receiver frame rate, CPU and GPU of NyrexVJ and of the receiver
manual.criteria: Proposed: picture upright and correct, receiver rate equals the output rate, sender reappears after a restart without restarting the receiver.

areas.title: Spout input from Unreal or Unity (Windows)

automated.note: feeds a generated pattern through the input path without Spout

manual.title: Spout input from a real sender
manual.needs: Windows PC with a Spout sender (Unreal with a Spout plugin, Unity or a test sender)
steps: Start the sender, then NyrexVJ.
Add the Spout source as a clip and play it.
Close the sender while playing, then start it again.
Run scripts/measure_live.py for 10 minutes.
manual.measure: Picture, behaviour when the sender disappears and returns, CPU, GPU, VRAM
manual.criteria: Proposed: picture correct, the clip falls back to its placeholder when the sender closes and recovers without restarting NyrexVJ.

areas.title: NDI output

automated.note: sends through the fake NDI library

manual.title: NDI output seen by a real NDI receiver
manual.needs: Two computers (or one with NDI Studio Monitor) on one network with the NDI runtime installed
steps: Turn NDI output on in NyrexVJ and select it in NDI Studio Monitor or OBS.
Play a look for 10 minutes while scripts/measure_live.py runs.
Unplug the network cable for 10 seconds and plug it in again.
manual.measure: Receiver frame rate, dropped frames at the receiver, CPU and GPU of NyrexVJ
manual.criteria: Proposed: receiver shows the picture, rate matches, the stream returns after the cable is plugged in.

areas.title: NDI input

automated.note: plays a test source through the whole live path

manual.title: NDI input from a real sender, with the sender lost and found again
manual.needs: A real NDI sender (OBS NDI plugin, a camera with NDI, another NyrexVJ) and the NDI runtime
steps: Add the NDI source as a clip and play it.
Run NyrexVJ --bench-live 300:ndi:NAME and keep the JSON.
Stop the sender for 30 seconds and start it again.
manual.measure: Latency and dropped-picture numbers from --bench-live, state shown in the Clip window
manual.criteria: Proposed: state goes to reconnecting and back to live without restarting NyrexVJ.

areas.title: Recording the final picture to a video file

automated.note: checks picture orientation, scaling, frame order, the GL state, backpressure, size changes and stalls of the live recording
records the output in every working format and reports capture time, encoder time, drops and file size

manual.title: Hardware encoders on a real graphics card
manual.needs: A graphics card with NVENC, Quick Sync or AMF and an FFmpeg with the matching encoder
steps: Open Settings, Recording and check that the hardware formats are listed.
Record two minutes at 1920 x 1080 and 60 frames per second with each hardware format and with H.264 software.
Play the files in a normal player and check picture, speed and file size.
manual.measure: Encoder name, frame time in NyrexVJ with and without recording, encoder load, dropped frames, CPU and GPU use
manual.criteria: Proposed: the hardware formats record without dropped frames, the frame time rises by less than 0.5 ms and the files play correctly.

manual.title: Recording next to VRChat
manual.needs: A computer that runs VRChat with the usual world and avatar load
steps: Start VRChat and NyrexVJ with the output on a second display.
Record ten minutes in H.264 and in HAP while the VRChat frame time is logged.
Compare the VRChat frame time with and without the recording.
manual.measure: VRChat frame time, NyrexVJ frame time, dropped frames, disk write rate
manual.criteria: Proposed: no frame drops in the recording and no visible change in the VRChat frame time.

manual.title: Sound and picture stay in sync over a long recording
manual.needs: A real audio input or system audio and a file player that shows both tracks
steps: Play a clip with a click track as audio source and record it for one hour.
Open the file and compare the click track with the picture of the clip at the start, the middle and the end.
Repeat once while the program is stalled on purpose for a few seconds.
manual.measure: Offset between picture and sound at the start, middle and end of the file
manual.criteria: Proposed: the offset stays below 40 ms for the whole hour.

manual.title: Full disk and unplugged drive
manual.needs: A small or nearly full drive and a removable drive
steps: Choose the small drive as recording folder and record until it is almost full.
Record to the removable drive and unplug it while recording.
Check the message in the program and open the files that were written.
manual.measure: Message shown, state of the program, state of the file
manual.criteria: Proposed: the program stays responsive, the recording ends with a clear message and the file that was written plays up to that point.

manual.title: Files after a crash
manual.needs: Players and editors the maintainer uses, for example VLC and DaVinci Resolve
steps: Record in H.264, ProRes and HAP with the crash-safe option on and end the program with the task manager.
Open every file in a player and in the editor.
Repeat with the crash-safe option off and note the difference.
manual.measure: Whether the file opens, how much of it plays, how long the editor needs to open it
manual.criteria: Proposed: with the option on, everything recorded up to a few seconds before the crash plays.

areas.title: Cameras and capture cards

automated.note: plays an FFmpeg test source as a camera

manual.title: A real camera or capture card, unplugged and plugged in while playing
manual.needs: A USB camera or a capture card and a cable
steps: Pick the device in the Clip window and play it.
Run NyrexVJ --bench-live 300:camera:NAME.
Unplug the device for 10 seconds while it plays, then plug it in again.
manual.measure: Format chosen by the driver, latency and dropped pictures from --bench-live, state after unplugging
manual.criteria: Proposed: picture shows, state goes to reconnecting and back to live, no crash.

areas.title: Several displays and projectors, hot plugging

automated.note: output windows, mapping and edge blending on the virtual display

manual.title: Fullscreen on a second display or a projector
manual.needs: A second display or a projector
steps: Add an output window in the Outputs panel, assign it to the second display and go fullscreen.
Run scripts/measure_live.py for 10 minutes.
Unplug the display cable for 10 seconds while the output runs, plug it back in and check the window.
manual.measure: Picture on the display, resolution and position, CPU and GPU, what happens to the window when the display disappears
manual.criteria: Proposed: picture correct at the display's native resolution, NyrexVJ keeps running while the display is missing.

areas.title: MIDI controllers and MIDI clock

automated.note: feeds one message through the real control path

manual.title: A real MIDI controller, unplugged and plugged in while running
manual.needs: A USB MIDI controller (pads or knobs) and, for the clock, a device that sends MIDI clock
steps: Map two controls in the MIDI panel.
Move them for one minute and check the response.
Unplug the controller, plug it in again and move the controls.
manual.measure: Response to controls, response after the device returns, clock tempo against the sender
manual.criteria: Proposed: mapped controls respond, the device is found again without restarting NyrexVJ.

areas.title: Art-Net / DMX output

manual.title: Art-Net to a real node or software receiver
manual.needs: An Art-Net node, HNode or QLC+ on the same network
steps: Set the same universe in NyrexVJ and the receiver.
Move a DMX channel in NyrexVJ and watch the receiver.
Run for 10 minutes and note whether the receiver stays in sync.
manual.measure: Channel values at the receiver, packet loss seen by the receiver
manual.criteria: Proposed: values at the receiver follow NyrexVJ without gaps.

areas.title: DJ sync: Pro DJ Link, MIDI clock, timecode

manual.title: Beat sync with a real player or mixer
manual.needs: A Pioneer player or mixer with Pro DJ Link (or a MIDI clock source) on the network
steps: Select the sync source in NyrexVJ and play a track.
Watch the beat indicator against the beat for 5 minutes.
Change the tempo on the player and stop the track.
manual.measure: Beat offset (by eye or with a recorded video), tempo shown in NyrexVJ against the player
manual.criteria: Proposed: beat indicator stays on the beat, tempo follows within one bar of a change.

areas.title: FFmpeg, hardware decoders and the fallback to the processor

automated.note: decodes the test clips with and without graphics card conversion
decode and upload times of one clip

manual.title: Hardware decoding on a real graphics card and the fallback
manual.needs: A graphics card with a hardware decoder (D3D11VA, DXVA2, NVDEC, VA-API or QSV) and an H.264/H.265 test clip
steps: Play the clip with --video-mode auto and note decoder and route in the Clip window.
Repeat with --video-mode software.
Play a clip with a profile the card does not support and check that the processor takes over.
manual.measure: Decoder name, decode time, CPU and GPU use for both modes
manual.criteria: Proposed: automatic mode uses the hardware decoder where available, the fallback shows its reason and playback continues.

areas.title: Plugin errors, limits and recovery

automated.note: loads and runs the example plugin
loads a plugin of the old interface version

areas.title: Long shows: frame times, memory growth, threads and handles over time

automated.note: short smoke run: events, samples and report; too short to judge growth
five minute run with the growth verdict; on software OpenGL only
parsers for nvidia-smi, Windows counters, PowerShell and amdgpu files with sample texts, plus a live check against the own process on Linux
checks this matrix, the results file and the table in docs/TESTING.md

manual.title: Three hour soak on a real graphics card
manual.needs: A PC with a real graphics card, the output resolution of the show and an idle desktop
steps: Run NyrexVJ --fresh --no-update-check --no-welcome --soak 10800 --bench-out soak.json.
In a second window run scripts/measure_live.py --seconds 10800 --out device.json.
Do not touch the PC while it runs.
manual.measure: growth block of soak.json (RSS, GPU estimate, threads, handles), over-budget frames, device.json VRAM curve
manual.criteria: Proposed: no leak verdict, VRAM of the whole card stays flat after the first 25 percent. The soak estimate counts only allocations the program makes itself; device.json is the check against drivers.

areas.title: Restart and recovery after a crash

automated.note: forces a crash and checks the recovery data
starts the program, ends it with kill -9, starts it again and checks that the second run works and ends its session cleanly

manual.title: End the program with the task manager during a show
manual.needs: Any PC
steps: Start NyrexVJ with a saved show, trigger a few clips.
End the process with the task manager (Windows) or kill -9 (Linux).
Start NyrexVJ again.
manual.measure: Time from start to the first picture, what is offered for recovery, state of the last saved show
manual.criteria: Proposed: the program starts, offers the recovery, and the saved show is intact.

areas.title: Running next to VRChat (CPU, GPU and VRAM shared)

manual.title: NyrexVJ and VRChat on the same PC with the show's setup
manual.needs: Windows PC with VRChat, a world with a Spout or NDI capture of NyrexVJ and a real graphics card
steps: Start VRChat in the world and NyrexVJ with the output going to the world.
Run scripts/measure_live.py --seconds 1800 --process NyrexVJ --process VRChat --out parallel.json.
Repeat with NyrexVJ closed to get the VRChat baseline.
manual.measure: CPU, GPU and VRAM of both programs and of the whole card, VRChat frame rate with and without NyrexVJ
manual.criteria: Proposed: the VRChat frame rate drops by less than the maintainer allows; the numbers go into the result either way.

areas.title: Media outages: file removed or truncated while it plays

automated.name: nvj_media_tests
automated.note: includes a video cut at open, cut while playing, overwritten while playing, deleted while playing and opened again after it came back

manual.title: Network share or external drive disappears during playback
manual.needs: A video on a network share or a USB drive
steps: Play the video from the share or drive.
Disconnect the share or drive for 10 seconds, then connect it again.
Trigger the clip again.
manual.measure: Picture while the media is gone, state shown, whether the clip plays again
manual.criteria: Proposed: no crash, no frozen program, the clip reports the problem and plays again after reconnecting.

areas.title: Web interface and REST API

automated.note: the interface through the real engine: off by default, token file, reads and writes, presets, stalled main thread, rate limit, lockout, new token, closed port
frame time with the interface off, idle, with polling clients and under a flood

manual.title: Control from a phone on the same network
manual.needs: A phone or tablet and a computer in the same Wi-Fi, the operating system firewall asking about the port
steps: Turn on the web interface and Allow other devices on the network.
Open the address with the IP address of the computer on the phone and paste the token.
Trigger clips, move the master and opacity sliders, load a look and press blackout while the show runs.
manual.measure: Whether every control reaches the program, the delay to the picture, touch behaviour of the sliders, the frame time of NyrexVJ with and without the phone connected
manual.criteria: Proposed: all controls work, the delay is below 300 ms, and the frame time rises by less than 0.2 ms.

manual.title: Windows sockets and the exclusive port
manual.needs: A Windows computer and a second program that tries to listen on the same port
steps: Turn on the web interface and open it in a browser on the same computer.
Start a second program that binds the same port and check that it fails.
Turn the interface off and on again several times and check the port is released.
manual.measure: Whether the page and the API answer, the error shown when the port is taken, whether the port is free after turning off
manual.criteria: Proposed: the page works, the second program cannot bind and the port is released at once.

manual.title: Hours of polling next to VRChat
manual.needs: A computer that runs VRChat and a second device that keeps the page open
steps: Start VRChat and NyrexVJ, turn on the web interface and open the page on a second device.
Run a --soak or a normal show for one hour with the page open and sliders moved now and then.
Compare the VRChat frame time and the memory of NyrexVJ with a run without the page.
manual.measure: VRChat frame time, NyrexVJ frame time, memory and handle growth, requests refused
manual.criteria: Proposed: no change in the VRChat frame time and no growth beyond the soak limits.

areas.title: ISF shader import: generators, image filters, several passes

automated.note: renders ISF generators, per cell values, image filters in the effect rack, a two pass blur, persistent buffers, compile error fallbacks, hot reload and the five example files through a real OpenGL context
adds the frame times of ISF generators and filters next to the plain Shader 2.0 cases

manual.title: Real ISF files from other programs on each graphics card vendor
manual.needs: A collection of ISF files made for VDMX, Resolume or Magic (generators and filters, at least 30, with and without several passes) and a graphics card of each vendor
steps: Copy the files into the shaders folder and watch the Library and the effect list.
Play every generator and put every filter on a layer with a picture, change every control, and read the notes in the Clip window.
Open the same files in the program they were made for and compare the pictures.
manual.measure: Files refused, files with notes, compile errors per driver, differences from the other program, visible glitches
manual.criteria: Proposed: every file that uses only supported features compiles on every vendor and looks the same as in the other program, and every file that does not says why.

manual.title: Heavy multipass filters and buffer memory at 1080p and 4K
manual.needs: A real graphics card, a tool that shows video memory (the driver panel or GPU-Z) and the filters isf_blur.fs and isf_trails.fs
steps: Put the blur and the trails filter on all four layers at 1920 x 1080, then at 3840 x 2160.
Read Settings, Performance (frame time, Shader buffers) and the video memory from the driver tool.
Switch decks and clear layers, and check that the memory goes back down.
manual.measure: Frame time, video memory by the driver, the value of the line Shader buffers
manual.criteria: Proposed: the frame time stays under the frame budget of the chosen rate, the program's number is within 10 percent of the driver's growth, and the memory is freed within a few seconds.

manual.title: Filter controls with audio, LFOs, macros and a MIDI controller during a show
manual.needs: A MIDI controller or the web interface, music as audio input and an ISF filter with four controls
steps: Put the filter on a layer and map its four controls to LFOs, audio bands and a macro.
Save a preset, restart and load it again, and check the values.
Turn the strength of the effect with the audio gate and play for ten minutes.
manual.measure: Whether the controls move the picture as the labels say, whether the preset restores them, frame time
manual.criteria: Proposed: all four controls follow their sources, the preset brings back the values and the picture, and the frame time does not rise during the run.

manual.title: File names with umlauts and spaces, hot reload on Windows
manual.needs: A Windows computer
steps: Copy ISF files with names like Größe Welle.fs and with spaces into the shaders folder.
Check the names in the Library and the effect list, save a change in an editor while the shader plays, and delete a file.
Save a preset that uses a filter, restart and load it.
manual.measure: Names shown, reload time, message after a delete, preset result
manual.criteria: Proposed: the names are right, a change shows within two seconds, a delete leaves a message and the picture stays intact.

areas.title: Show timeline: keyframe lanes, cues on a ruler, timecode following, hand moves

automated.note: opens the timeline window and runs 60 frames through a real OpenGL context; a smoke test of the window, not a test of its use

manual.title: Following a real LTC or MTC source: start, jump, loss and return
manual.needs: A DAW or timecode generator that sends LTC to an audio input or MTC to a MIDI port, and a timeline with at least three lanes and five cues
steps: Set Settings, Sync to the source, turn the timeline on and play the DAW from the start; watch the lanes and the cues.
Jump around in the DAW (forwards, backwards, to the start), and read the counters Jumps and Cues skipped.
Stop the timecode for 10 seconds with Hold the position, then with Keep running on its own transport, and start it again at another time.
manual.measure: Position error against the DAW in frames, cues fired twice or missed, whether the lanes take the new value at once after a jump, behaviour at loss and return
manual.criteria: Proposed: the position stays within two frames of the source, no cue fires twice, cues after a jump are skipped and counted, lanes chase within one frame, and a lost timecode behaves as the chosen policy says.

manual.title: Hand moves with a MIDI controller or the web interface during playback
manual.needs: A MIDI controller or a phone with the web interface, and a timeline with lanes on layer opacity and master level
steps: Play the timeline on its own transport and move a controlled slider with the controller.

Check that the lane shows Moved by hand and the timeline stops writing to it, then wait for the next keyframe segment (policy Until the next keyframe segment) or press Release (policy Until I release it).
Repeat with a lane on a toggle such as blackout and with two lanes moved at once.
manual.measure: Time between the move and the lane letting go, any visible fight between hand and lane, state after release
manual.criteria: Proposed: the lane lets go within two frames, the picture never flickers between the two values, and the lane takes over again exactly as the policy says.

manual.title: Window, keys and files on Windows
manual.needs: A Windows computer
steps: Open the window from the menu and with --timeline; add lanes and keyframes, use Space, Home, Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y with the window focused and with another window focused.
Change something, end the program with the task manager within half a second and again after two seconds, and start it again.
Replace timeline.json by a damaged file and start the program.
manual.measure: Which keys act where, what timeline.json holds after each kill, whether timeline.json.damaged appears and the timeline starts empty
manual.criteria: Proposed: Space is tap tempo and undo is the composition's whenever the timeline window is not focused, the file is always whole (old or new), and a damaged file is kept as a copy.

manual.title: A long show with a looping timeline next to VRChat
manual.needs: A real graphics card, VRChat, a timeline with 16 or more lanes and a loop, and scripts/measure_live.py
steps: Run the timeline in its loop for two hours with the output on, VRChat open and measure_live.py sampling NyrexVJ and VRChat.
Compare the frame time and memory with the same show with the timeline off.
Look at the counters at the end.
manual.measure: Frame time and its spread, memory growth, writes and hand moves counters, any missed loop wrap
manual.criteria: Proposed: no measurable cost beyond the spread of the baseline, no memory growth beyond the growth check of the soak test, and every loop wrap counted.

areas.title: User manual and website: the manual window, the generated website, the pictures, English and German text

automated.note: the generated website pages are current, the Python and the C++ parser give the same outline for the fixture, English and German have the same structure, and every link, anchor and picture exists; no script, no foreign host, no picture without alt, width and height
opens the manual window at the first chapter and runs 60 frames through a real OpenGL context; a smoke test of the window, not a test of its use
opens the German manual at a chapter by its id and runs 60 frames; checks that a chapter id of --manual is found

manual.title: The German manual read by a native speaker next to the program
manual.needs: A native German speaker who has used NyrexVJ, the German interface, and the manual in the window and on the website
steps: Read every chapter in the manual window with the interface set to German, and open each place the text names (a menu, a window, a setting) to see that the name and the described behaviour are right.
Mark every sentence that sounds like a translation, every wrong or missing interface name, and every claim about the program that is not true.
manual.measure: Number of wrong interface names, wrong statements and unnatural sentences per chapter
manual.criteria: Proposed: no wrong interface name and no wrong statement remains; unnatural sentences are fixed by the reader or listed in the issue.

manual.title: The manual window on Windows with a real graphics card
manual.needs: A Windows 10 or 11 PC with a graphics card, a 1920 x 1080 and a 1280 x 720 screen or window, and display scaling of 100 and 150 percent
steps: Open the manual from Help, User manual and with F1, search for a word, open a hit, follow a link between chapters, press Back, and use the previous and next chapter buttons.
Make the window narrow and wide, change the display scaling, and read the chapters with the longest tables (Settings reference, Keyboard shortcuts, The command line) in English and in German.
Start with --manual outputs and with --manual outputs/<section id> and check the page that opens.
manual.measure: Text that is cut off or overlaps, tables that are unreadable, links that do not work, frame time while the window is open
manual.criteria: Proposed: all text is readable at both sizes and both scalings, every link and the Back button work, and opening the window does not change the frame time by more than the noise of the measurement.

manual.title: The website in real browsers, on a phone, with the keyboard and in print
manual.needs: Firefox, Safari or Edge on a desktop, a phone with a browser (iOS or Android), and a screen reader if one is available
steps: Open the start page, the contents of the manual, a chapter with pictures and the one-page version in English and in German, at desktop and at phone width.
Go through a chapter with the keyboard only, and with a screen reader if one is available; check the contents, the links, the pictures and their descriptions.
Print a chapter and the one-page version, or save them as PDF.
manual.measure: Layout breaks, overlapping or cut-off text, unreachable links, missing alt texts, page breaks in the printout
manual.criteria: Proposed: no layout break at 360 px or wider, every link is reachable with the keyboard, every picture has a useful description, and the printout is readable.

manual.title: The statements about hardware and other programs in the manual, checked with the real devices
manual.needs: A MIDI controller, OBS with Spout, an NDI source or receiver, a camera or capture card, an LTC or MTC source, an Art-Net or DMX device, and VRChat with a VRSL world
steps: Follow the chapters Control, Live sources, Outputs, Show sync, Stage and Recording step by step on the real devices.
Write down every step that does not work as described, every missing step and every statement about a device, a menu in another program or VRChat that is wrong.
manual.measure: Number of wrong or missing steps per chapter, with the device and its version
manual.criteria: Proposed: every step works as written, or the chapter says that it was not tried.

areas.title: Live workflow: launch quantize, favorites and tags, replace everywhere, MIDI feedback, controller profiles

automated.note: every new text of the quantize menu, the library popups and the MIDI feedback and profile page has a translation in all seven tables, with the same printf specifiers

manual.title: MIDI feedback to a real pad controller on Windows
manual.needs: A MIDI controller with lit pads or motor faders that has an output port, Windows, and a mapping of clips, a column, a deck, blackout and one fader
steps: Tick Send feedback to the controller, choose the output with the name of the controller and start clips, a column and a deck; watch the pads.
Switch blackout, bypass and solo from the program and from the controller, and move the mapped fader by hand and by the program.
Unplug the controller while feedback is on, then plug it in and press Refresh devices.
manual.measure: Which pads light and go dark correctly, the delay between a change and the light in milliseconds (a phone camera at 240 frames a second is enough), whether a motor fader fights a moving hand, and what the page shows after the unplug
manual.criteria: Proposed: pads follow the state within two frames, a fader does not fight the hand, no message loop or crash after the unplug, and the page shows the error. Colour or note values that a specific controller needs for other colours are written down, not guessed.

manual.title: Launch quantize against a real beat in a real show
manual.needs: A beat source (a DJ player with Pro DJ Link, MIDI clock or audio with a steady beat), a screen or an output on a projector, and a deck with a column of clips
steps: Set Quantize to Beat, then Bar, press cells and a column a little before and after the beat, and film the screen and the speaker together.
Remove the beat source while clips are waiting, and look at the counter and the launches.
Hold the program paused and press a cell.
manual.measure: Time between the grid line and the first frame of the new clip in milliseconds, launches that start at a wrong time, behaviour when the beat source disappears
manual.criteria: Proposed: a launch starts within one frame of its grid line, launches never wait for a beat that is not coming, and a pause or a lost clock starts them at once.

manual.title: Favorites, tags and replace everywhere with a real library
manual.needs: A library with at least 500 clips and media files, and a show with several decks that use the same video in many cells
steps: Mark favorites, add tags to 50 clips, search with a word, with tag: and with is:fav, and restart the program.
Replace one video that plays in many cells of several decks with another, with and without keeping the playback settings, then undo.
Copy a controller profile to another computer and load it there.
manual.measure: Whether the search feels instant with 500 clips, whether every cell of every deck changed, whether the undo restored all of them, and whether the profile loaded on the other computer
manual.criteria: Proposed: search needs no visible wait, no cell keeps the old clip, one undo restores all of them, and the profile loads with every mapping.

areas.title: Show packages: export, import, dry run, path repair, rollback, the Show package window

automated.note: every text of the Show package window and every message of the package and workflow code has a translation in all seven tables, with the same printf specifiers
opens the Show package window on the Export tab and runs 40 frames through a real OpenGL context; a smoke test of the window, not a test of its use

manual.title: A real show moved from one Windows computer to another and back
manual.needs: Two Windows computers (or two user accounts) with NyrexVJ, a real show with video clips, 3D models, own shaders, a node effect, a venue setup and a cue list, and a USB stick
steps: Export the show with all of it, write a source or licence note for two files, and carry the package on the stick.
On the other computer open Import show package, read the plan, import with Keep mine, and open the show.
Change one media file on the second computer and import again with Keep both and then with Replace, and look in show_backups.
Export from the second computer and import on the first.
manual.measure: Time to pack and to import in seconds, the size of the package against the size of the files, whether every cell plays the same clip as before, whether the licence notes appear, and what show_backups holds
manual.criteria: Proposed: no cell is empty that was not reported missing, no file outside the data folder is touched, Keep both leaves both files and the show uses the new one, Replace leaves the old file in show_backups, and the second round trip gives the same show.

manual.title: A package of several gigabytes on a slow USB stick and a network drive
manual.needs: A show with at least 8 GB of video, a USB stick of USB 2 speed, and a network drive
steps: Export to the stick and to the network drive and cancel one export half way.
Import from each, cancel one import half way, and import once with the stick removed half way.
Watch whether the program keeps drawing and the progress bar moves.
manual.measure: Seconds for each step, the frame rate of the program while a job runs, and whether a cancelled or interrupted run leaves a .part or .nyxshow-new file or a half imported show
manual.criteria: Proposed: the program never freezes, a cancelled write leaves no file, a cancelled or interrupted import leaves the data folder as it was (the window says everything was put back), and the free space check refuses a destination that is too small before any copy starts.

manual.title: Clicking through the Show package window
manual.needs: The program on Windows with a mouse and the English and the German interface
steps: Open File, Export show package and File, Import show package, drop a .nyxshow file on the window, and drop a .nyxclip file.
In Export tick and untick presets and venue setups, press Check what goes in, write notes and licence texts, and press Create the package.
In Import try a missing file, a file that differs, Find missing files with a folder, and Open the show.
manual.measure: Anything that is cut off, overlaps, cannot be clicked, shows an English text in the German interface or a wrong state
manual.criteria: Proposed: every button and checkbox does what its text says, a dropped .nyxclip is not taken for a show package, and no text is cut off at the default window size and at 125 and 150 percent scale.

areas.title: Community packages: .nyxpack, versioned manifest, dependencies, conflicts, plugin consent, update, removal and rollback, the Community packages window

automated.note: every text of the Community packages window and every message of the package code has a translation in all seven tables, with the same printf specifiers
opens the Community packages window on the Install tab and runs 40 frames through a real OpenGL context; a smoke test of the window, not a test of its use

automated.command: NyrexVJ --pack-build FOLDER FILE, --pack-info FILE, --pack-install FILE (twice), --pack-remove ID
automated.note: builds a package from a folder, shows it, installs it, installs it again unchanged and removes it in a scratch data folder; checks exit codes and that the files appear and move to package_backups

manual.title: A real plugin installed from a package on Windows: consent, left off, switched on by hand, update and removal
manual.needs: A Windows computer with NyrexVJ, the example plugin from plugins/example built as a .dll and packed with plugin.json into a .nyxpack, and a second version of the same package
steps: Open the package, read the warning for a native plugin, try to install without the tick and then with it.
Open Settings, Plugins and check that the plugin is listed and switched off, then switch it on and use one of its sources.
Install the second version while the plugin is on, then switch it off and install again, and remove the package.
Let the plugin crash on purpose, restart, and install the package again.
manual.measure: Whether any step switched the plugin on by itself, the state of plugins/config.json and plugins/disabled.json before and after each step, whether the old library was moved to package_backups, and what the window said at each refusal
manual.criteria: Proposed: the plugin is never on after an install, config.json and disabled.json are unchanged by every install, update and removal, an update with the plugin on is refused with a clear message, and a plugin in safe mode stays in safe mode.

manual.title: The window used with a mouse on a real data folder with own files
manual.needs: A computer with NyrexVJ and a data folder with own presets, shaders and node effects, and two packages by other people (one with files of the same names as your own, one that needs the other)
steps: Install the dependent package first and read the message, then the other one, then the dependent one.
Install the package with the same file names and try Keep my files, then Replace my files, and look in package_backups.
Edit a shader that came from a package, update the package and remove it, and read what was kept.
Drop a .nyxpack file and a .nyxshow file on the window.
manual.measure: Whether every message can be understood without reading the manual, whether any file of yours changed without being asked, what package_backups holds, and how long Check package takes on a package of 200 MiB
manual.criteria: Proposed: no file of yours is changed or lost without the choice Replace, the file you edited is kept on removal and named, a show package is refused with a message that says it is a show package, and the window stays responsive while a package is read.

manual.title: Packages from a USB stick and a network drive, cancelled and interrupted
manual.needs: A package of about 200 MiB on a USB stick and on a network drive
steps: Check and install from each.
Cancel one install half way and pull the stick during another.
Look at the plugins, presets, shaders and package_backups folders and the packages folder afterwards.
manual.measure: Seconds for each step, leftover temporary files, and whether the record exists for a package that was not completely installed
manual.criteria: Proposed: a cancelled or interrupted install leaves the folders as they were and no record, and the window says so.

areas.title: Text clips, limited particle clips and effect chains: fonts and Unicode, transparency, audio and beat modulation, particle limits, damaged files, chain save, search, preview, export and import

automated.note: in the real engine with OpenGL: text and particle clips draw, the background is transparent and the layer below stays visible, audio and beat change size and particle count, the same start gives the same picture hash, the particle limit holds and is clamped, a very long text stays inside the atlas limit, damaged files and an unknown font do not stop the show, a broken shader pair does not stop the show and recovers; the benchmark times a flat layer, a text layer and four particle limits
compiles the text and particle programs and waits for the text atlases of the built-in clips
every text of the Text and particles window, the Effect chains window and the settings has a translation in all seven tables, with the same printf specifiers
opens the Text and particles window on the Text tab (1 selects the Particles tab) and runs 40 frames through a real OpenGL context; a smoke test of the window, not a test of its use
opens the Effect chains window for the first layer and runs 40 frames through a real OpenGL context; a smoke test of the window, not a test of its use

manual.title: Text and particle cost on a real graphics card
manual.needs: A Windows or Linux computer with a graphics card, NyrexVJ, and the output resolution you use for shows
steps: Run NyrexVJ --generator-selftest 120 --bench-out result.json and keep the file.
In a show, play a text clip with the Wave animation above a heavy 3D clip and read the GPU time in the status bar with and without the text.
Play the Confetti clip with the particle limit at 2048, 8192 and 16384 and read the GPU time and the frame rate at each setting.
manual.measure: Milliseconds per frame of the self test, the GPU time of the status bar with and without the clips, and the frame rate at each particle limit
manual.criteria: Proposed: a text layer adds under 0.5 ms and the particle limit of 2048 under 0.5 ms on a graphics card of the last five years, 16384 under 2 ms, and the frame rate holds the target in every case.

manual.title: Fonts and characters on your own computer
manual.needs: A computer with NyrexVJ and a few fonts of your own (a script font, a heavy display font, a font with Japanese characters) in the fonts folder
steps: Write a text with umlauts, accents, Greek, Cyrillic, a Japanese word and a music note in each font and look at the preview.
Save the text, put it on a layer above a video and switch the animations one after the other with music playing.
Remove a font file while a text that uses it is playing and save the text again.
manual.measure: Which characters are shown as a question mark, whether the note about missing characters appears, how long the first picture of a long text takes, and what the clip shows when the font is gone
manual.criteria: Proposed: characters that the font has are drawn correctly, characters it lacks are marked and the window says so, and a missing font changes to a default font without stopping the layer below.

manual.title: The windows used with a mouse during a show
manual.needs: A computer with NyrexVJ, an audio source and a MIDI controller or mouse
steps: Edit a text and a particle clip while the show runs and save both, then look at the clips on the layers.
Save a chain from the master, apply it to a layer, undo it, search for it by an effect name, preview it and export it to a USB stick.
Import the file again on a second installation, including one with an effect that does not exist there.
manual.measure: Whether anything stutters while a window is open, whether Undo restores the old effects, and what the import window says about the missing effect
manual.criteria: Proposed: no dropped frames while the windows are open, one Undo step restores the effects, and the missing effect is named while the other effects are kept.

areas.title: GPU particles with transform feedback and a processor fallback: card against processor reference, repeatability, ring reuse, memory budget, every fallback, audio and beat modulation, state left clean

automated.note: in the real engine with OpenGL: the shaders compile, the card matches a processor reference of the same algorithm and itself bit for bit, another seed and louder audio change the result, every beat adds one burst, the ring reuses the oldest slots, the memory budget cuts, refuses and returns, every fallback (setting off, shader fault, budget too small) runs the clip on the processor and the clip returns to the card, no GL state is left behind, the pictures are visible and repeat, the engine switches without a restart; the benchmark times the update step and the draw at 1920 x 1080 and 3840 x 2160 for 16,384 to 1,048,576 particles
every text of the Graphics card section, the GPU settings and the fallback messages has a translation in all seven tables, with the same printf specifiers
opens the Particles tab on the GPU Nebula clip with the setting on and runs 40 frames through a real OpenGL context; a smoke test of the window, not a test of its use

manual.title: GPU particle cost on a real graphics card
manual.needs: A Windows or Linux computer with a graphics card (the card and driver version are part of the result), NyrexVJ and the output resolution you use for shows
steps: Run NyrexVJ --gpu-particle-selftest 8 --bench-out result.json and keep the file. A failed check of the card against the processor reference is a result too.
Turn on Settings, Performance, Experimental GPU particles, play GPU Nebula on a layer above a heavy clip and read the GPU time in the status bar with and without it.
Raise the Particle pool of GPU Nebula in the Particles tab step by step to 1,048,576 with a budget of 64 MB and read the GPU time and the frame rate at each step.
manual.measure: The update and draw milliseconds of the self test at 1080p and 4K, the GPU time of the status bar with and without the clip, the frame rate at each pool size, and whether any check failed
manual.criteria: Proposed: the checks pass, a pool of 262,144 adds under 2 ms of GPU time at 1080p on a graphics card of the last five years, a million particles stay under 8 ms, and the frame rate holds the target in both cases. If the numbers are worse, the budget default and the limits are to be revisited.

manual.title: The fallback on a real computer
manual.needs: A computer with NyrexVJ and, if you have one, a second computer with an older or integrated graphics card
steps: With GPU particles on, play GPU Beat Burst with music and turn the setting off and on again while it plays.
Set Graphics memory for GPU particles to 8 MB, play GPU Nebula and look at the message under the preview and the pool.
On the older or integrated card run the self test and play GPU Nebula.
manual.measure: Whether the clip keeps playing when the setting changes, what the window says when the budget is too small, and which checks pass on the older card
manual.criteria: Proposed: the clip never stops or leaves a black picture when the setting changes, the budget message names the cause, and on a card without transform feedback or with a failed check the clip plays on the processor and the window says why.

manual.title: A show with GPU particles on the beat
manual.needs: A computer with NyrexVJ, an audio source with a beat, and the output setup you use for events
steps: Play GPU Beat Burst and GPU Rain on two layers over a video for 30 minutes with the audio running and the beat clock locked.
Watch the memory page of Settings, the GPU time and the dropped frames, and switch the output resolution once.
Save a GPU clip of your own with a different pool and seed, restart NyrexVJ and play it again.
manual.measure: The graphics memory counted for Text and particles at the start and the end, the number of dropped frames, and whether the saved clip looks the same after the restart
manual.criteria: Proposed: the memory stays inside the budget and does not grow, no dropped frames that were not there without the clips, and the saved clip starts from the same seed and looks the same on the same computer.

areas.title: Graphics memory diagnostics: driver readout kept apart from the estimate, P95 and P99, dropped frames, upload traffic, eight warnings with hysteresis, an optional memory budget that releases only idle clips by priority and never a playing one, the pressure ladder and its recovery

automated.note: in the real engine with OpenGL: eight images of 3584 x 3584 pixels are imported and loaded with the budget off, a budget of 256 MB releases the idle ones and keeps the playing and the next one, a released image loads again when launched, turning the budget off restores the old behaviour, four playing layers push the pressure to step 4 with layers at half resolution and the playing images kept, the warning logic reports resident memory over the budget, the pressure comes back to step 0 once the layers are cleared, the upload counter matches a known byte count and the engine reports it, the driver readout is plausible or rejected, no GL state is left behind; the probe images are removed again; the benchmark compares the frame time with the budget off and on
every text of the Graphics memory and traffic block, the warnings and the new settings has a translation in all seven tables, with the same printf specifiers
opens the Performance page with the new block in a real OpenGL context and writes a picture; a smoke test of the window, not a test of its use

manual.title: The driver readout on a real graphics card
manual.needs: A Windows or Linux computer with an NVIDIA or AMD graphics card (card and driver version are part of the result), NyrexVJ, and another program that uses video memory such as VRChat
steps: Open Settings, Performance and read Measured by the graphics driver with only NyrexVJ running, then start VRChat in a heavy world and read it again.
Run NyrexVJ --gpu-diag-selftest 5 --bench-out result.json and keep the file; a failed check of the driver readout is a result too.
Compare the in use number with the one the operating system shows for the card (Task Manager on Windows, nvidia-smi or the vendor tool on Linux).
manual.measure: Total, free and in use video memory in NyrexVJ and in the operating system tool with and without VRChat, whether the eviction count ever rises, and whether any check of the self test failed
manual.criteria: Proposed: the driver block is filled, total and free match the operating system tool within a few percent, free memory drops when VRChat starts, and no check fails. If the numbers differ strongly, the readout or its wording is to be revisited.

manual.title: The memory budget with a VRChat like load
manual.needs: A computer with a graphics card and NyrexVJ, a show with more clips (images, videos and 3D scenes) than fit your budget, and VRChat or a similar game running at the same time
steps: Set a Memory budget a little under what the estimate shows with every clip loaded, tick Release clips that are not in use when over the budget and play through the clips for 30 minutes.
Watch the estimate, the released count, the pressure step, the warnings and the frame rate, and launch a clip that was released a while ago.
Tick Also lower the layer resolution, set a budget below what the playing layers need and watch the steps up and back down.
manual.measure: The estimate against the budget over time, how many clips were released, how long a released clip takes to show after its launch, the P99 and the dropped frames with the budget off and on, and the pressure steps
manual.criteria: Proposed: the estimate stays inside the budget, a playing clip is never released, a released clip shows within a quarter of a second at the longest, the dropped frames do not rise with the budget on, and the steps come back down when there is room. If a launch shows a visible gap, the idle time of 5 s or the preparation of the next clips is to be revisited.

manual.title: The warnings in a show
manual.needs: A computer with NyrexVJ, a show with video and live sources, and the output setup you use for events
steps: Play the show for 30 minutes with the warnings on and look at the status bar and the Warnings list.
Start a second heavy program, or raise the output resolution, until a frame time warning should appear.
Change Warning limits and watch the warning appear and go away.
manual.measure: Which warnings appeared and when, whether each matched what you saw on the output (stutters, dropped frames), how long a warning stayed after the cause was gone, and the upload rate with the live sources running
manual.criteria: Proposed: a warning appears when the output visibly stutters and not when it does not, it goes away within about six seconds after the cause is gone, it never flickers, and the upload number is plausible for the sources in use.

areas.title: Shader editor with a live preview: text editing with undo and redo, highlighting, compiler messages on their lines, a compile that waits for typing to stop and never blocks, the last working version kept on every failure, an isolated preview that never touches a playing clip, a cost control, templates, safe saving as a shader asset with a conflict check and hot reload

automated.note: in the real engine with OpenGL: valid and broken shaders (parser error, compile error, link error, empty text, text over the limit), the last working version kept and still drawn after each, recovery, the four templates compile and draw, a buffer shader with its memory counted, a refused buffer budget and its recovery, a filter file that is not previewed, a heavy shader that the cost control slows and pauses, Resume, an output clip that keeps its own shader while the preview shows another, everything released when the playground is not requested, save as a shader asset, the folder scan and hot reload, a changed disk version detected before saving, the other program's file left alone, a name that leaves the folder and a text over the limit refused; the benchmark compares the frame time with the playground off, with a light preview and with a heavy preview

drives the editor window with real key, character and mouse events: typing, a typed mistake shown on its line while the preview keeps the last working picture, undo and redo, comments, a selection that typing replaces, Ctrl+S with a name and Enter, a change by another program loaded when nothing is unsaved, and the conflict dialog with unsaved edits (nothing written before the decision); about 50 s on a software renderer
every text of the editor window has a translation in all seven tables, with the same printf specifiers
opens the editor on a broken shader in a real OpenGL context and writes a picture; a smoke test of the window, not a test of its use

manual.title: Compiling and previewing on real graphics drivers
manual.needs: A Windows or Linux computer with an NVIDIA, AMD or Intel graphics card (card and driver version are part of the result) and NyrexVJ
steps: Open Creator, Shader editor and note whether the window says that the driver compiles in the background or on the spot.
Paste a large shader (several hundred lines, or a Shadertoy shader with many loops), press Compile now and watch the frame time on the Performance page while it compiles.

Break the shader in five ways (a missing semicolon, an unknown function, a wrong type, a missing main, a link error such as an unwritten input) and check that each message is on the right line, that the last working picture stays, and that the log of the driver is complete.
Run NyrexVJ --shader-editor-selftest 60 --bench-out result.json and keep the file.
manual.measure: Whether the parallel compile is reported, the time a large shader takes to compile, the longest frame while it compiles, whether each of the five mistakes is reported on the right line, and whether any check of the self test failed
manual.criteria: Proposed: the output keeps its frame rate within the noise while a shader compiles in the background, every mistake is on the right line, the last working version stays on screen, and no check fails. A driver that compiles on the spot is allowed to stutter for the time of the compile, and the window must say so.

manual.title: Editing while a show is running
manual.needs: A computer with a graphics card, NyrexVJ with a deck that plays a shader clip on a layer, an output window or projector, and optionally VRChat running
steps: Open the shader file of the playing clip with Edit in shader editor, put the output on a second display and start playing.
Type a change, then a mistake, then fix it, while watching the output.
Make the shader very heavy (a loop with several thousand steps) and watch the preview and the output.
Save the file and watch the clip reload.
manual.measure: Whether the output ever changed or dropped frames while the editor compiled or previewed, how long the preview took to be slowed down and stopped, and whether the saved change reached the clip
manual.criteria: Proposed: the output does not change until you save, typing and compiling cause no visible stutter, the preview is slowed or stopped and the output stays smooth, and the saved change appears in the clip within about a second. A frozen driver on a shader that never ends is a known limit and is to be written down, not hidden.

manual.title: Saving and conflicts on Windows with cloud sync or antivirus
manual.needs: A Windows computer with the data folder inside a cloud synced folder (OneDrive, Dropbox) or a virus scanner that scans on write
steps: Open a shader file in the editor, change it and save it a few times in a row.
Change the same file in another editor while it is open in NyrexVJ, with and without unsaved edits in NyrexVJ, and check the conflict dialog.
Open the file in another program that locks it and save from NyrexVJ.
Delete the file in Explorer while it is open.
manual.measure: Whether a save ever failed or left a partial file, whether the conflict dialog came up when it should and only then, and what the message said when the file was locked or deleted
manual.criteria: Proposed: no partial file is ever left, the conflict dialog appears exactly when the content on disk differs from what was loaded, a locked file gives the message that another program may have it open, and a deleted file can be written again. Any other behaviour is to be written down.

manual.title: Typing: layouts, input methods and the clipboard
manual.needs: A computer with a keyboard layout that uses dead keys (for example German or French) and, if possible, a Japanese or Chinese input method, NyrexVJ
steps: Type text with umlauts and accents in a comment, with Ctrl+/ and undo around it.
Copy a block from another program, paste it into the editor, copy a block from the editor and paste it elsewhere.
With an input method, compose a word in a comment and confirm it.
manual.measure: Whether every character arrives as typed, whether the clipboard works in both directions on Windows and Linux, and whether composing text works
manual.criteria: Proposed: finished characters arrive correctly and the clipboard works in both directions. Composing text with an input method is not expected to work yet and the result is to be written down.

areas.title: Video routing: route clips that play a layer, a group of layers or the master (same frame, or the previous frame as feedback), loops refused, GPU only copies with a memory limit and release, copies for each deck of a transition, sender sources for Spout, NDI and the recording, and the Video routing window

automated.note: in the real engine with OpenGL, with pixel checks: a faded out layer shown through a route clip, a routed picture pixel for pixel equal to the layer and with its transparency kept, two layers using one source, a chain of routes, a group of layers (added on top it doubles), the master from the previous frame, feedback exactly one frame late and its transparent first frame, three loops refused and reported, a missing and a bypassed source, switching between a route, a feedback route and a plain clip every frame for 120 frames, a source layer stopped and started every frame, a resolution change (same frame route there at once, feedback restarts), sender sources (a layer, a group, a source that is not playing, back to the master, a feedback source refused), the small previews and their release, the memory of one picture and the release after 90 frames, a transition whose outgoing deck keeps its routes, nothing allocated without routing; the benchmark compares four shader layers, three plus a route layer, and one and two sender copies
every text of the Video routing window and the Routing filter has a translation in all seven tables, with the same printf specifiers
builds a composition with route clips, opens the window in a real OpenGL context and writes a picture; a smoke test of the window, not a test of its use

manual.title: Cost and memory on a real graphics card
manual.needs: A Windows or Linux computer with an NVIDIA, AMD or Intel graphics card (card and driver version are part of the result), NyrexVJ at 1920 x 1080 and at the largest composition size you use
steps: Load a composition with four shader or video layers and note the frame time and the graphics memory on the Performance page.
Replace the fourth layer by Route: Group 1-3, then by Feedback: Layer 1, and note both numbers again for each.
Choose Layer 1 for Spout and Layers 1-3 for NDI in Output, Video routing, start both senders and note both numbers again.
Run NyrexVJ --routing-selftest 120 --bench-out result.json and keep the file.
manual.measure: The frame time and the graphics memory in every step, the memory per copy, and whether any check of the self test failed
manual.criteria: Proposed: a route layer costs about what a simple shader layer costs, a sender copy costs well under a millisecond on a card, the memory grows by one picture per routed source (two for a feedback source) and falls back about a second and a half after the last user, and no check fails. Numbers worse than that are to be written down.

manual.title: A routed picture seen by OBS and by an NDI receiver
manual.needs: A Windows computer with OBS and the Spout2 plugin, and a second program or computer that receives NDI
steps: Put a different clip on each layer, choose Layer 1 for Spout and Layers 1-2 for NDI, and start both senders.
Check in OBS that the Spout picture is layer 1 alone, without the master effects, and that the NDI receiver shows the mix of layers 1 and 2.
Stop the clip of layer 1 (empty the cell) and watch both receivers, then put it back.
Set both senders back to Master and check that the full picture is back and that the memory of the copies falls.
manual.measure: What each receiver showed in each step, whether the picture was opaque, whether a stopped source gave black, and whether the frame rate of the receivers changed
manual.criteria: Proposed: the receivers show exactly the chosen layer or group, an empty source sends black and says so in the window, choosing Master brings back the whole picture, and the frame rate does not change.

manual.title: Recording a routed source and routing across a deck change
manual.needs: A computer with a graphics card, NyrexVJ, a player for the recorded file and a deck set with route clips on two decks
steps: Choose Layer 1 for Recording in Output, Video routing, record about 30 seconds and open the file.
Play deck 1 with a route clip in layer 2 and Feedback: Layer 1 in layer 3, switch to deck 2 with a transition of 3 seconds and back, and watch the output.
Change the resolution of the composition while a feedback layer plays.
manual.measure: What the recorded file shows, whether the routed layers kept their picture during the transition and after it, and whether any frame was black or wrong
manual.criteria: Proposed: the file shows layer 1 only, the outgoing deck keeps its routes while it fades out, a feedback layer needs one frame to restart after a deck switch or a resolution change, and nothing else goes wrong.

manual.title: A long show with four routed layers
manual.needs: A computer with a graphics card, a deck that routes all four layers (for example the Video routing demo), an output window or projector and about two hours
steps: Start the demo composition with --routing-demo or build the same by hand and let it run with the Performance page open.
Every ten minutes change the route clips of two layers and the sender sources, and note the graphics memory estimate and, where the driver reports it, the free video memory.
After two hours note whether the memory grew and whether the frame time changed.
manual.measure: The memory estimate and the frame time at the start, every ten minutes and at the end, and any warning of the Performance page
manual.criteria: Proposed: the estimate returns to its starting value after every change, the frame time stays within the noise, and no warning stays on.

areas.title: Network sync: one master and followers over UDP with a signed protocol, a state snapshot with incremental updates, sequence numbers, packet loss and reconnect, a clock estimate for the beat and the timecode, missing media shown instead of sent, version negotiation, and the Network sync block on the Sync page

automated.name: nvj_netsync_tests
automated.note: the protocol with a simulated network: signature, sequence numbers, duplicates, reordering, loss, handshake retries, versions, resync, reconnect and the clock estimator

automated.name: nvj_netsync_show_tests
automated.note: the state vector of 159 values, deltas, the manifest and the conflict rules

automated.name: nvj_netsync_transport_tests
automated.note: the same protocol over real UDP sockets on the loopback interface, the key file and the limit per address

in the real engine, in both roles, with a relay that drops, delays and duplicates packets: controls, decks, clips, beat, tempo, pause, timecode cues, missing media, a different version, a wrong key, a flood, and the cost of the update step; it replaces the key file for the run and puts it back

two real NyrexVJ programs on one computer (master and follower over UDP on the loopback interface), a calm phase, then 25 percent loss and up to 25 ms jitter, a 6 s outage and a reconnect, with the beat of both compared by wall clock and every synced control compared at the end
every text of the Network sync block has a translation in all seven tables, with the same printf specifiers

manual.title: Master and follower on two computers in a real network
manual.needs: Two computers with NyrexVJ in the same network (a wired switch, then Wi-Fi), the same version on both, the same media files (a show package) and a firewall you can open for UDP port 9030
steps: On the first computer choose Role Master, tick Allow other PCs in the network and copy the key.
On the second choose Role Follower, type the IPv4 address of the first, paste the key and compare the Key check code.
Run the same deck on both, move faders and colours on the master, switch decks and start clips, change the tempo and pause.
Unplug the cable of the follower for 10 seconds and plug it back in. Then do the same with the Wi-Fi switched off and on.
Run NyrexVJ --netsync-report report.json on the follower with --run-seconds 300 and keep the file.
manual.measure: The status on the follower in every step, how long it took to reach In sync and to recover, how far the two outputs differ when you film both screens with a camera at 60 frames a second, and the clock offset, round trip and jitter on the page
manual.criteria: Proposed: the follower reaches In sync within a few seconds, follows every change within about a quarter of a second, says Master lost after the unplugging and comes back by itself within the backoff of 5 s, the two outputs differ by no more than about one frame, and no value ends up different on the two computers.

manual.title: Three or more followers and the limit of eight
manual.needs: Three to nine computers with NyrexVJ in one network, or several programs on a few computers
steps: Connect one follower after the other to one master and note the status and the CPU use of the master on the Performance page.
Move several faders and run an effect with a lot of changes for ten minutes.
Connect a ninth follower and read what it says.
Press New key on the master and watch every follower.
manual.measure: The status of every follower, the frame time of the master with one, four and eight followers, the packet counters on the page, and what the ninth follower said
manual.criteria: Proposed: the master serves eight followers without a visible change in its frame time, a ninth is refused with a reason, and after New key every follower stays out until it has the new key.

manual.title: Windows at run time
manual.needs: A Windows 10 or 11 computer, NyrexVJ 0.48.0 or later and a second computer (any system) with the same version
steps: Use the Windows computer as master and then as follower with the second computer.
Check that the Windows firewall asks for the permission and that the port can be opened.
Look at the permissions of the netsync_key file in the data folder.
Run NyrexVJ --netsync-selftest --bench-out result.json with NYREXVJ_DATA_DIR set to an empty folder.
manual.measure: Whether the connection works in both directions, what the firewall asked, who can read the key file, and whether every check of the self test passed
manual.criteria: Proposed: both directions work, the key file is readable only by your own account as far as the system shows, and the self test passes.

manual.title: Different versions, a wrong key and a hostile network
manual.needs: Two computers, an older and a newer NyrexVJ version, and a third computer or a script that sends packets
steps: Connect the older and the newer version and read what the follower shows.
Use a wrong key on the follower and read both pages.
Send garbage and the packets of a valid session with changed bytes to the port of the master from the third computer.
Send many thousands of packets a second for a minute.
manual.measure: What each page showed, whether the master answered anything to a packet with a wrong signature, the frame time of the master while it was flooded, and whether the show was changed
manual.criteria: Proposed: a different control list gives Clock only with the reason shown, a wrong key gives no answer and a clear message on the follower, forged and changed packets change nothing, and the flood is limited to 400 packets a second for each address without a visible effect on the output.

manual.title: A long show with a follower
manual.needs: Two computers with graphics cards, a real show with video and 3D layers on both, and about two hours
steps: Run the show with the Performance page open on both and the network sync on.
Every ten minutes change decks, start clips and change the tempo on the master.
Restart the follower once and the master once during the show.
Run NyrexVJ --netsync-report with --run-seconds 7200 on the follower.
manual.measure: The frame time on both, the clock offset and its change over two hours, the number of resyncs, mismatches and lost periods in the report, and whether the beat drifted
manual.criteria: Proposed: no drift beyond the frame time over two hours, no growth in memory, every restart ends in In sync by itself, and the report lists only the differences of media you know about.

areas.title: Hot standby: a primary and a standby PC with readiness checks, health reports, a takeover by hand or automatic, a leader epoch against two leaders, a held output on the standby, and the Hot standby window

automated.name: nvj_failover_tests
automated.note: the readiness checks, the fingerprint of the show, the state machine of the standby (wait, loss, manual and automatic takeover, the blockers, the confirmation window) and the measured times

automated.name: nvj_netsync_tests
automated.note: protocol version 2: the readiness and health tail on Clock and Ping, an old peer that never sees it, the signed Takeover message with its epoch rule, no reply loop between two masters and the Bye reason

in the real engine: readiness, a held and really black output, a primary that falls silent after ten seconds of readiness and the automatic takeover with its measured times, the leader serving a new follower, the notice to the old primary, a step down for a higher epoch, a clean close without automatic takeover, a takeover by hand, and a clip that cannot be decoded; it uses a temporary data folder

two real NyrexVJ programs on one computer: a frozen primary (SIGSTOP, a network partition) and the automatic takeover, the old primary stepping down after SIGCONT, a kill of the leader (SIGKILL) and the automatic takeover by the former primary, and a clean close followed by a takeover by hand

automated.name: nvj_control_tests
automated.note: the four hot standby settings and the leader port with their defaults and ranges
every text of the Hot standby window has a translation in all seven tables

manual.title: Two computers in a real network: pulled cable, closed program and crashed program
manual.needs: Two computers with NyrexVJ 0.49.0 or later in the same wired network, the same media files, one projector or monitor on each, UDP port 9030 open
steps: Turn on Use hot standby on both, set one to master and one to follower, copy the key and wait until the standby has been ready for ten seconds.
Pull the network cable of the primary for 10 seconds and plug it in again.
End the primary through the task manager (a crash) and watch the standby.
Start the primary again as a follower of the new leader.
Repeat with the automatic takeover off and press Take over by hand.
manual.measure: Seconds from the event to the first picture on the standby (film both screens at 60 frames a second), the numbers under Last takeover, whether both screens ever showed a picture at the same time, and what the old primary did when it came back
manual.criteria: Proposed: the standby takes over within the set time plus about two seconds, the old primary steps down after the cable is back, no value of the show is older than the set time, and nothing opens or switches without the setting that allows it.

manual.title: Seamless switching with a video switcher or router
manual.needs: Two NyrexVJ computers and a video switcher, matrix or router (or an NDI router) that your venue uses, with one input for each computer
steps: Send the output of both computers into the switcher and the switcher into the projector.
Let the primary play, take over by hand on the standby and switch the switcher to the standby input at the same moment.
Repeat the switch with the standby input already selected as a preview and with an automatic takeover.
manual.measure: The length of the black or frozen picture on the projector, filmed at 60 frames a second or more, and the offset between the beat on both computers
manual.criteria: Proposed: no black picture longer than the switching time of the switcher itself, and a beat that jumps by less than a quarter of a beat.

manual.title: A real decoder or output failure on the standby
manual.needs: A standby computer with a video file that you can damage, a graphics card and a projector
steps: Make the standby play a clip, then rename or damage the file on the standby only.
Watch the readiness table and the primary, then stop the primary and watch the standby.
Close the output window of the standby and look at the table again.
manual.measure: Which check changed, how long it took, what the primary showed about the standby, and whether the standby took over by itself
manual.criteria: Proposed: the table names the problem within a few seconds, the primary shows that the standby is not ready, and the standby does not take over by itself while it is not ready.

manual.title: Windows at run time
manual.needs: Two Windows 10 or 11 computers with the same version
steps: Run NyrexVJ --failover-selftest --bench-out result.json with NYREXVJ_DATA_DIR set to an empty folder.
Do the steps of the first test with the Windows firewall asking for the permission once on the new leader port.
Run scripts/test_failover_two_instances.py if Python is installed (it uses SIGSTOP and SIGKILL, which only exist on Linux and macOS, so on Windows use the Task Manager by hand).
manual.measure: Whether every check of the self test passed, what the firewall asked, and the times under Last takeover
manual.criteria: Proposed: the self test passes, the leader port can be opened and the takeover works in both directions.
